practiceQuestions.q: In which year was the voting age in India reduced from 21 years to 18 years by amending Article 326 of the Constitution?
practiceQuestions.sol: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 (came into force in 1989) reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years.

practiceQuestions.q: Which constitutional amendment act reduced the voting age in India to 18 years?
practiceQuestions.sol: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 amended Article 326 to lower the voting age.

practiceQuestions.q: Who heads the Delimitation Commission in India?
opts: A retired Judge of the Supreme Court
practiceQuestions.sol: The Delimitation Commission is appointed by the President of India and works in collaboration with the Election Commission of India. It is headed by a retired Supreme Court judge.

practiceQuestions.q: What does NOTA stand for in the context of Indian elections?
opts: National Organization for Transparency and Accountability
practiceQuestions.sol: NOTA stands for 'None of the Above', introduced following the Supreme Court's 2013 judgment to allow voters to reject all candidates.

practiceQuestions.q: VVPAT stands for:
opts: Voter Verification and Poll Accountability Test
practiceQuestions.sol: VVPAT stands for Voter Verified Paper Audit Trail, which allows voters to verify that their vote was cast correctly.

practiceQuestions.q: Which committee recommended state funding of elections in India?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Indrajit Gupta Committee on State Funding of Elections (1998) explicitly recommended state funding of elections in-kind to curb black money.

practiceQuestions.q: The maximum limit of election expenditure for Lok Sabha candidates is prescribed by:
opts: Central Government (Ministry of Law and Justice)
practiceQuestions.sol: The expenditure limit is fixed by the Central Government (under Rule 90 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961), though it is recommended/reviewed in consultation with the Election Commission.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the cooling-off period before the end of election campaigning (silence period) mandated under Section 126 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951?
practiceQuestions.sol: Section 126 prohibits public meetings, processions, and use of electronic media for election campaign during the 48 hours ending with the hour fixed for the conclusion of the poll.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following bodies recommended the establishment of a multi-member Election Commission in 1989/1990?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Dinesh Goswami Committee on Electoral Reforms (1990) recommended making the Election Commission a multi-member body.

practiceQuestions.q: The use of Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) was first introduced on an experimental basis in which year?
practiceQuestions.sol: EVMs were first used in 1982 in the Paravur assembly constituency of Kerala on an experimental basis.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the 1996 amendment to the Representation of the People Act, 1951 change the dynamic of electoral campaigning and contesting?
opts: It banned independent candidates from contesting elections entirely.
It reduced the number of proposers needed for recognized political party candidates to one and banned candidates from contesting from more than two constituencies.
It allowed foreign funding for domestic political parties.
It introduced compulsory voting for all citizens.
practiceQuestions.sol: The 1996 amendment restricted candidates from contesting from more than two constituencies, increased security deposits to deter non-serious candidates, and reduced the proposer requirement to 1 for party candidates.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary rationale behind the Supreme Court's landmark 2003 judgment mandating disclosure of criminal antecedents, assets, and educational qualifications by candidates?
opts: To implement complete state funding of elections
To uphold the voter's Fundamental Right to Know under Article 19(1)(a) for informed voting
To ban political parties with criminal office-bearers
To disqualify any candidate charged with a bailable offense
practiceQuestions.sol: The Supreme Court held that the voter's right to know about the antecedents of candidates is an integral part of freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a).

practiceQuestions.q: What change was introduced regarding casual vacancies in Parliament and State Legislatures through the 1996 amendments to the RP Act, 1951?
opts: By-elections must now be held within six months of the occurrence of the vacancy, except when the remainder of the term is less than a year.
Casual vacancies can remain vacant until the next general election without restrictions.
Nominated members replace elected members instantly.
practiceQuestions.sol: Section 151A was added in 1996 requiring by-elections to fill casual vacancies within six months, unless the remainder of the term is less than one year or the Election Commission certifies difficulty.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the introduction of Electoral Bonds (now struck down by the Supreme Court) impact the transparency of political funding?
opts: It mandated full public disclosure of all corporate donors and their contribution amounts on a live portal.
It introduced complete anonymity for donors, shielding identity from the public and removing corporate donation limits, which the Supreme Court later ruled violated the right to information.
It completely banned foreign contributions to political parties.
It permitted only cash donations through registered banking channels.
practiceQuestions.sol: Electoral bonds brought anonymity, removed limits on corporate funding, and removed the requirement for companies to disclose political donations in their profit and loss accounts, which the Supreme Court struck down in 2024 as unconstitutional.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the significance of the Lily Thomas v. Union of India (2013) judgment regarding convicted legislators?
opts: It struck down Section 8(4) of the RP Act, 1951, ending the 3-month protection period for convicted MPs/MLAs to appeal, leading to immediate disqualification upon conviction.
It granted immunity from arrest to all sitting parliamentarians during budget sessions.
It made criminal defamation a non-cognizable offense for politicians.
It allowed convicted politicians to contest elections if they appeal within 30 days.
practiceQuestions.sol: Lily Thomas judgment declared Section 8(4) ultra vires, meaning MPs and MLAs convicted with a sentence of 2 years or more are disqualified immediately upon conviction, with no 3-month grace period for appeal.

practiceQuestions.q: Why are Exit Polls restricted during ongoing multi-phase elections in India?
opts: To protect media channels from financial losses
To prevent early projections and exit poll results from unduly influencing the voting behavior of electors in subsequent phases.
To prevent political parties from funding private survey agencies
Because exit polls are universally banned by the Constitution under Article 324
practiceQuestions.sol: Section 126A of the RP Act, 1951 restricts conducting and publishing exit polls during the period notified by the ECI to ensure voters in later phases are not psychologically swayed by trends from earlier phases.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the structural role and significance of the Model Code of Conduct (MCC)?
opts: It is a statutory law enacted by Parliament backed by severe criminal penalties.
It is a set of guidelines agreed upon by political parties, enforced largely through moral sanction, persuasion, and ECI's persuasive/administrative authority.
It is a constitutional amendment article that regulates party splits and mergers.
It is a judicial decree issued exclusively by the Supreme Court bench during general elections.
practiceQuestions.sol: MCC is not statutory law; it is a consensus document of guidelines evolved by the ECI in consultation with political parties to ensure a level playing field during elections.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the 2002 amendment regarding criminal declarations (under Supreme Court directions) transform candidate nominations?
opts: It made filing criminal affidavits mandatory for every candidate, revealing pending criminal cases and convictions.
It prohibited individuals with petty fines from contesting local body elections.
It gave police officials the power to screen and reject nomination papers.
It exempted national party leaders from declaring their assets.
practiceQuestions.sol: Following SC directives, Section 33A was inserted into the RP Act in 2002, requiring candidates to submit an affidavit detailing pending criminal cases, convictions, assets, and liabilities.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the core objective behind lowering the age limit for enrolment in electoral rolls via the 2012 amendment to registration rules?
opts: To enable youth to register as soon as they turn 18, introducing multiple qualifying dates instead of a single cut-off date.
To allow minors aged 16 to vote in municipal elections.
To eliminate senior citizens from the rolls automatically.
To implement compulsory voting for college students.
practiceQuestions.sol: Subsequent reforms introduced multiple qualifying dates (instead of just January 1st) so that young citizens attaining 18 years could register without waiting for the next calendar year.

practiceQuestions.q: In the context of electoral reforms, what does the term 'Paid News' refer to, and how has the ECI addressed it?
opts: Official government advertisements promoting voting awareness funded by the ECI.
Any news or analysis published in print or electronic media in exchange for money or valuables to covertly promote a candidate, treated as election expenditure.
Legal payments made to journalists for covering rallies fairly.
State funding provided to news agencies during election campaigns.
practiceQuestions.sol: Paid news distorts the level playing field. The ECI tracks it as undeclared election expenditure and has recommended making it an electoral offense under the RP Act.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Election Commission of India and Electoral Reforms:
1. The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 lowered the voting age for Lok Sabha and Legislative Assembly elections from 21 to 18 years.
2. The Dinesh Goswami Committee (1990) recommended state funding of elections in cash to all political parties.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct (61st Amendment, 1988). Statement 2 is incorrect because state funding in-kind was recommended by the Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998), and cash funding was generally opposed due to misuse risks; Dinesh Goswami focused on regulation, EVMs, and anti-defamation/corruption measures.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) and VVPAT in India:
1. EVMs were used across all constituencies in the Lok Sabha elections for the first time in 2004.
2. VVPAT slips are mandatory to be counted for 100% of EVMs in every constituency as per Supreme Court directions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: 2004 Lok Sabha elections saw 100% EVM usage. Statement 2 is incorrect because VVPAT slips are verified randomly (traditionally 5 per assembly segment, later affirmed by SC as random verification protocols, not 100% count of all VVPAT slips).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Model Code of Conduct (MCC):
1. The MCC comes into operation immediately once the Election Commission announces the election schedule.
2. The MCC contains elaborate constitutional provisions enforceable directly under Article 324.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: MCC applies as soon as election dates are announced. Statement 2 is incorrect because MCC has no statutory or constitutional backing of its own; it is a code of ethics agreed upon by parties, though violations can attract action under specific penal laws (IPC, RP Act).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding disqualification of legislators:
1. Under the Representation of the People Act, 1951, a person convicted of any offense and sentenced to imprisonment for not less than two years is disqualified from contesting elections.
2. The disqualification ceases immediately upon filing an appeal in a High Court against the conviction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct under Section 8(3) of RP Act, 1951. Statement 2 is incorrect because as per the Lily Thomas judgment (2013), mere filing of an appeal does not stay the disqualification unless the appellate court explicitly stays the conviction itself (not just the sentence).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about NOTA (None of the Above) in Indian elections:
1. NOTA was introduced pursuant to the Supreme Court judgment in People's Union for Civil Liberties (PUCL) v. Union of India (2013).
2. If NOTA receives the highest number of votes in a constituency, the election is automatically countermanded and the candidate with the second-highest votes is barred from future elections.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct (PUCL 2013 judgment). Statement 2 is incorrect because even if NOTA gets the highest votes, the candidate with the next highest valid votes wins; NOTA currently has no legal power to nullify an election or disqualify runners-up.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indrajit Gupta Committee on State Funding of Elections (1998):
1. It recommended complete state funding of private political rallies in cash.
2. It concluded that state funding of elections is desirable and recommended it in-kind rather than in cash.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect (it opposed cash funding). Statement 2 is correct: the committee recommended partial state funding in-kind (such as free fuel, electoral rolls, printing, media time) due to the economic condition of the country.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the powers and composition of the Election Commission of India (ECI):
1. Since 1993, the ECI functions as a multi-member body comprising a Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners.
2. The Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners enjoy unequal constitutional protection regarding removal from office.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The multi-member format became permanent via Act in 1993. CEC can be removed only via impeachment (like SC judge), whereas other Commissioners can be removed by the President upon the recommendation of the CEC.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding candidate expenses and declarations in Indian elections:
1. The ceiling on election expenditure is fixed by the Election Commission of India for all parliamentary and assembly constituencies.
2. Candidates are required to file an affidavit disclosing their criminal antecedents, assets, liabilities, and educational qualifications at the time of filing nominations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because expenditure limits are fixed by the Central Government under the Conduct of Elections Rules, not directly by the ECI (though ECI recommends/reviews). Statement 2 is correct (mandatory affidavit under RP Act and SC rulings).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the disqualification under the Tenth Schedule (Anti-Defection Law) added by the 52nd Amendment Act, 1985:
1. A legislator is disqualified if they voluntarily give up membership of their political party or vote/abstain contrary to party whip directions without prior permission.
2. The decision on disqualification under the Tenth Schedule rests with the Election Commission of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because the decision on anti-defection is made by the Chairman or Speaker of the House, not the Election Commission (though the Speaker's decision is subject to judicial review).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding electoral reforms and the Prevention of Insults to National Honours Act / RP Act provisions:
1. Section 123 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 defines 'corrupt practices', which include appeals to vote or refrain from voting on the grounds of religion, race, caste, community, or language.
2. The Supreme Court in 2017 clarified that an appeal by a candidate or their agent to vote for or against a candidate on the ground of the voter's religion, race, caste, community, or language constitutes a corrupt practice.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Section 123(3) covers religious/caste appeals, and the landmark 2017 Supreme Court judgment (Abhiram Singh v. C.D. Commachen) interpreted it strictly to include the voter's religion/caste as well, reinforcing secularism in elections.
